---
title: "Fish Abundance Over Time"
format: pdf
---

```{r}
# loading in packages 
library(tidyverse) # general use
library(janitor) # cleaning data 
library(here) # data organization 
library(lubridate) # date and time 

fish <- read.csv(here("data", "Annual_fish_comb_20260923.csv"))
```

```{r}
#| label: transforming-data-frame

# creating new object, fish_clean
fish_clean <- fish |> 
  # cleaning the names
  clean_names() |> 
  # renaming the date column to original_date
  rename(original_date = date) |> 
  # filtering to remove the no count data, -99999
  filter(count >= 0) |> 
  # using mutate and lubridate to convert original_date into new date column that can be used to create time series
  mutate(
    date = ymd(original_date)) |> 
  # relocating columns to to left to be easier to look at
  relocate(date, count, common_name, site)
```

```{r}
#| label: exploring-fish-by-abundance

# creating new vector, fish_species
fish_species <- fish_clean |> 
  # selecting for common_name
  select(common_name) |> 
  # unique to drop name repeats 
  unique() |>  
  # using pull to extract column as a vector
  pull()
# viewing vector 
fish_species


# creating top_species_table 
top_species_table <- fish_clean |> 
  # grouping by species 
  group_by(common_name) |>  
  # summarize to make one row per species 
  # sum to get the total fish count of each species
  summarize(total_count = sum(count)) |> 
  # ungrouping the data 
  ungroup() |> 
  # ranking from most to least abundant 
  arrange(desc(total_count)) |> 
  # selecting top 5 species 
  slice_head(n = 5)

# creating top_species_vector
top_species_vector <- top_species_table |> 
  # using pull to extract column as a vector
  pull(common_name)
```
